Names are case-insensitive, and spaces or hyphens may stand in for underscores (`"Krackhardt kite"` works as well as `"krackhardt_kite"`). | Name | Nodes | Edges | Description | |------|------:|------:|-------------| | `bull` | 5 | 5 | A triangle with two pendant horns | | `butterfly` | 5 | 6 | Two triangles sharing one node (the bowtie) | | `chvatal` | 12 | 24 | Smallest triangle-free 4-regular graph needing 4 colors | | `cubical` | 8 | 12 | Skeleton of the cube, the 3-dimensional hypercube | | `desargues` | 20 | 30 | Cubic symmetric; Levi graph of the Desargues configuration | | `diamond` | 4 | 5 | Complete graph K4 with one edge removed | | `dodecahedral` | 20 | 30 | Skeleton of the dodecahedron | | `franklin` | 12 | 18 | Cubic bipartite graph that embeds on the Klein bottle | | `frucht` | 12 | 18 | Smallest cubic graph with no symmetry | | `grotzsch` | 11 | 20 | Smallest triangle-free graph needing 4 colors | | `heawood` | 14 | 21 | The (3,6)-cage, Levi graph of the Fano plane | | `hoffman_singleton` | 50 | 175 | The (7,5)-cage, a 7-regular Moore graph of diameter 2 | | `house` | 5 | 6 | A square with a triangular roof | | `house_x` | 5 | 8 | The house graph with both diagonals of the square | | `icosahedral` | 12 | 30 | Skeleton of the icosahedron | | `krackhardt_kite` | 10 | 18 | Network where degree, betweenness, closeness disagree | | `mcgee` | 24 | 36 | The (3,7)-cage, the smallest cubic graph of girth 7 | | `moebius_kantor` | 16 | 24 | Cubic symmetric; generalized Petersen graph GP(8,3) | | `nauru` | 24 | 36 | Cubic symmetric; generalized Petersen graph GP(12,5) | | `octahedral` | 6 | 12 | Skeleton of the octahedron, K(2,2,2) | | `pappus` | 18 | 27 | Cubic symmetric; Levi graph of the Pappus configuration | | `petersen` | 10 | 15 | The (3,5)-cage, a common counterexample in graph theory | | `sedgewick_maze` | 8 | 10 | Small maze from Sedgewick's Algorithms | | `shrikhande` | 16 | 48 | Strongly regular, like the 4 x 4 rook's graph but not it | | `tetrahedral` | 4 | 6 | Skeleton of the tetrahedron, the complete graph K4 | | `truncated_cube` | 24 | 36 | Skeleton of the truncated cube | | `truncated_tetrahedron` | 12 | 18 | Skeleton of the truncated tetrahedron | | `tutte` | 46 | 69 | Cubic, planar, 3-connected graph with no Hamiltonian cycle | | `tutte_coxeter` | 30 | 45 | The (3,8)-cage, Levi graph of Cremona-Richmond | Where NetworkX has the same graph, the node numbering matches its numbering, with node `0` there being the first node created here (NetworkX labels the Shrikhande graph's nodes `(x, y)`, which is node `4x + y` here); the cubic Hamiltonian graphs follow their LCF notation (see `add_lcf_graph()`), so their first `n` edges in order form a Hamiltonian cycle. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Named graphs are useful for: - checking algorithms against published values (the Petersen graph has chromatic number `3`, girth `5`, and 120 automorphisms) - counterexamples: the Tutte graph refutes Tait's conjecture, and the Frucht graph is cubic with no symmetry at all - small, recognizable examples for teaching and documentation ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the graph, from the table above. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `name=` is not one of the names above. The error message lists the valid names. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The Petersen graph has `10` nodes and `15` edges, every node has degree `3`, and its shortest cycle has length `5`: ::: {#1d472f36 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec petersen = ec.Graph().add_named_graph("petersen") petersen.count_nodes(), petersen.count_edges(), petersen.girth() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (10, 15, 5) ``` ::: ::: In Krackhardt's kite, the most central node depends on the measure: node `"4"` has the highest degree, while node `"8"` lies on the most shortest paths: ::: {#12a572ab .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} kite = ec.Graph().add_named_graph("Krackhardt kite") degree = kite.degree_centrality(return_dict=True) betweenness = kite.betweenness_centrality(return_dict=True) ( kite.get_label_from_id(max(degree, key=degree.get)), kite.get_label_from_id(max(betweenness, key=betweenness.get)), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ('4', '8') ``` ::: ::: The Tutte graph is cubic, planar, and 3-connected, yet it has no Hamiltonian cycle, which disproved Tait's 1884 conjecture that every such graph has one: ::: {#f7118825 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} tutte = ec.Graph().add_named_graph("tutte") degrees = tutte.get_node_df()["degree"].unique().to_list() degrees, tutte.is_planar(), tutte.node_connectivity() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ([3], True, 3) ``` ::: :::
